hero.title: The Wormhole alternative
hero.body: Wormhole nailed encrypted, link-based sharing in the browser. BIShare does the same — end-to-end encrypted links, up to 100 GB, no account — and goes further with native apps and instant nearby transfer that works fully offline, device to device, no server in the middle.

why.title: Why choose BIShare over Wormhole?
why.body: Wormhole is a great encrypted-link tool, but it lives entirely in the browser and always needs a network path between sender and receiver. BIShare adds two things: real apps for iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows, and Linux, and true offline nearby transfer — when both devices are on the same Wi-Fi or a hotspot, the file goes straight across with no internet and no server at all.

0.b: Send a link for files up to 100 GB, end-to-end encrypted with the key kept in the link fragment so our servers only see ciphertext. The recipient opens it in any browser and the file decrypts locally.

1.b: On the same network, BIShare transfers device to device with no upload — end-to-end encrypted, no size cap, and it works over a hotspot with no internet connection.

2.b: iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows, and Linux get real apps — faster nearby transfers, background sending, and the full feature set, not just a browser tab.

0.q: What is a good Wormhole alternative?
0.a: BIShare. It offers the same end-to-end encrypted, account-free link sharing Wormhole is known for, and adds native apps plus instant nearby transfer that works fully offline.

1.q: Is BIShare end-to-end encrypted like Wormhole?
1.a: Yes. Encrypted share links keep the key in the link fragment, so the server only ever stores ciphertext. Nearby transfers are encrypted device-to-device and never reach a server at all.

2.a: Yes — this is the big difference. When both devices are on the same Wi-Fi or a phone hotspot, BIShare transfers directly with no internet and no cloud, something a browser-only tool like Wormhole can't do.

3.q: How large a file can I send?
3.a: Encrypted links carry up to 100 GB free. Nearby device-to-device transfers have no size cap, because the file is never uploaded.

4.a: No. Sending and receiving need no sign-up. Share a link, QR code, or 6-character code, and the recipient opens it in any browser.
